### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 287fd6e5d054b9b1efa80f08f9e5be609edb32c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d4f411b218e7d1b70ba0f82ff5aa04287ea4c504` — the merge of head `e10a433726204b9a93358021a4a8d68218b8f211` into base `287fd6e5d054b9b1efa80f08f9e5be609edb32c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d4f411b218e7d1b70ba0f82ff5aa04287ea4c504 && git checkout d4f411b218e7d1b70ba0f82ff5aa04287ea4c504
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 287fd6e5d054b9b1efa80f08f9e5be609edb32c2 e10a433726204b9a93358021a4a8d68218b8f211 && git checkout -B drift-repro 287fd6e5d054b9b1efa80f08f9e5be609edb32c2 && git merge --no-ff e10a433726204b9a93358021a4a8d68218b8f211

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 287fd6e5d054b9b1efa80f08f9e5be609edb32c2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e10a433726204b9a93358021a4a8d68218b8f211`
Local-runs: none

PR #23130 for card #23042, read on 2026-10-13T03:01Z: the card body and all 4 comments (triage `6124786465`, claim `6126172325`, `os-dev-report` `6137194016`, seat ACCEPT `6137230536` — the last judged independently, not adopted), the PR body, its 3-file list, the net diff against `main` (the GitHub diff is byte-identical, modulo index lines, to `git diff` from the merge base bcebd8409, and `origin/main` at 287fd6e5d has not moved either non-changeset file since that base, so the net diff is exactly these 3 files, +127/−34), and the 39 check-runs on the head. Sentences were verified against `origin/main` and the fetched head read-only. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface movement the diff implies, each judged:

- **`packages/spec/src/conversions/types.ts` (+17/−5): TSDoc only, on `RetiredConversionState.retiredAfter`.** The member's type `${number}.${number}.${number}` is unchanged (head line 297); `RetiredConversionState` is file-internal (no `export`, line 232) and reaches consumers only through the exported union `MetadataConversion` (line 313, re-exported by `conversions/index.ts:24`). No Zod schema, JSON Schema, runtime code, `api-surface` file (`git grep retiredAfter` in `packages/spec/api-surface` at the head: no hit) or generated artifact moves. The only published movement is the doc comment inside `dist/*.d.ts` (`dist` is in `files[]`). **Accept set: unchanged — right. Public surface: text only — right.**
- **`retired-after.census.test.ts` (+105/−29): a repository test, not shipped** (`files[]` publishes `dist`, `json-schema`, `liveness`, `prompts`, `src/**/*.zod.ts` and the listed docs; no test file). The rule it now enforces, read off the code rather than the report:
  - `atOrBelowLabel(v, label)`: a stable label `x.y.z` admits `v` at or below `x.y.z`; a prerelease label `x.y.z-PRE` admits only `v` strictly below `x.y.z`. It bounds all three label comparisons: census well-formedness (line 178), "never above the package label" (line 190) and the UNPUBLISHED range (line 140).
  - `unpublishedStampProblem(v, label, lastCensused)`: under a **stable** label the two old branches survive with identical predicates — the exact-label branch when the census has caught up (`cmp(release, lastCensused)` at or below 0, which is the old `!pending`), else the inclusive range `[lastCensused, x.y.z]`; the failure strings are the old strings. Under a **prerelease** label the exact-label branch is never taken (the census holds stable releases only, so its tarball is never censused) and the range is `[lastCensused, x.y.z)`: `x.y.z` is refused now, and the newest published stable release passes. **This is exactly the card's ruled direction** (triage `6124786465`: under a pre-mode label a new retirement stamps the newest published stable release, never the label; the interim range excludes the prerelease's own release triple, so `18.0.0` is refused now; nothing changes under a stable label). **Right.**
  - Extending the strict reading to the well-formedness and "never above the label" checks (the dev's deviation 1) is **right, not scope creep**: with the range check alone, `18.0.0` under `18.0.0-next.N` would still pass the check titled "never above the package label", and a censused `18.0.0` beside a prerelease label is a contradiction the well-formedness check should name.
- **Could a test or gate pass while the rule is wrong?** Today's label is stable (`17.7.0`, `pre.json` is `mode: pre` / `tag: next` but no version pass has run), so the real-registry checks exercise only the stable arm. The prerelease arm is reached by the three new simulated-label pins, which call the same two functions the real checks call (not copies), on `18.0.0-next.0` and `18.0.0-next.12`: `18.0.0` and `18.0.1` refused, `17.4.0`/`17.7.0`/`17.7.1` admitted, the exact-label branch never taken even with the census at `17.7.0` or `18.0.0`. The dev's two ablations (strict arm relaxed to inclusive; `!prerelease` guard dropped) each went red, so the pins bind the production predicates. A stable-label regression is bound by the inclusive/exact pin. The only unpinned text is the `PRERELEASE` message suffix, on which no verdict depends. **No green-while-wrong path found.**
- **The artifact door is not touched and needs no change.** Its window (`metadata-core/src/artifact-forward-conversion.ts:37-38`) replays an entry when `floor` is at or below `E.retiredAfter`, or when `floor = M.0.0` and `E.toMajor = M`. Every entry on `main` stamped `17.7.0` (5 of 117 retired entries, all 5 `toMajor: 18`) replays for a `^18` floor through the major-step arm whatever its stamp, and the door's own module docblock already assumes a prerelease retirement is "stamped at or below" the last release of the previous line — the very rule this PR states. The unreleased `.changeset/23001-prerelease-artifact-window.md` on `main` says the same ("every retirement that lands during the v18 prerelease is stamped with the last 17.x release"). **Consistent.**
- **Real registry today: no verdict changes** (stable label; the dev's byte-identical stable-label failure lists at `17.4.0` and `17.7.0`; `src/conversions` 448/448 at the head per the report). The first pre-mode label will be the first real exercise of the prerelease arm; the pins already hold it.
- **Shipped sentences, all consistent with each other and with the rule.** TSDoc (stable label: the label itself; prerelease label: the newest published stable release, below `x.y.z`, never the label and never `x.y.z`; `17.7.0` under `18.0.0-next.N`; PUBLISHED entries: the stable release just before the first tarball carrying them retired; a `17.x` maintenance release during the prerelease becomes the value on census refresh), the census docblock (same, plus the `[last censused release, release triple)` tolerance) and the changeset (same) agree. The maintenance-release clause is right by the census mechanics: the committed census is held in ascending semver order (well-formedness check), so a `17.7.1` published without the retirement sorts just before `18.0.0` and becomes "just before the first tarball that carries it retired", and the door's triple comparison opens for a `^17.7.1` floor as it should. ADR-0087's amended definition ("the last published `@objectstack/spec` whose authoring surface still accepted the old shape") agrees. One non-blocking wording note: the TSDoc lead "read off the package's version label" is literal only for the stable case; the bullets that follow make the prerelease case explicit, so no reader is misled.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `.changeset/23042-retired-after-prerelease-stamp.md`: `@objectstack/spec: patch` — right.** The diff publishes one thing: a doc comment inside the shipped `.d.ts` files (the dev measured the old sentence at 2 dist files before and 0 after). That is a published change, so `skip-changeset` would be wrong; nothing an author can write moves, so `minor` is not owed. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.
- **`Clause-②: no` — right.** The published accept set does not change: the `retiredAfter` type is unchanged, no schema or runtime moves, and the census test is unpublished. The PR body carries the claim's `Clause-②: no` line verbatim on line 2, with no `(widening)`/`(narrowing)` arm — well-formed. `check:adr-0087-registration` owes nothing here: a non-breaking changeset is outside that gate (its G1 case), so no disposition marker is required, and none is present.
- **Changeset text is correct.** It names the public member as `MetadataConversion.retiredAfter` (the exported name; the file-internal interface would be the wrong name for a CHANGELOG reader), states both label cases and the maintenance-release case exactly as the TSDoc does, and ends "Text only: `retiredAfter` keeps its `${number}.${number}.${number}` type, and the accepted set does not change" — true.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared. The dev's `deviations` and `out_of_scope_findings` (report `6137194016`), each answered:

Deviations
1. All three label comparisons bound by `atOrBelowLabel`, not only the pending branch — **accepted as necessary** (see ①; otherwise `18.0.0` passes under the "never above the label" title).
2. Whole spec `local` project cut by the foreground cap at the final head, measured 659/659 at the branch commit 2e7bb5fb2 — **accepted**: the merge commit at the head changed none of this diff's files (verified: `origin/main` differs from the merge base at neither `retired-after.census.test.ts` nor `types.ts`), and `Test Core (1–6/6)` runs on the head are CI's. In progress at read time; see the gate reading below.
3. First ablation run void (repo-relative path, no file selected), re-run counted — **procedural, no effect on the diff**.
4. `git fetch --depth=1` of a fixture commit for a self-test prerequisite — **procedural; adds objects, rewrites no ref**.
5. Presence probe spelled with values masked — **procedural; not verifiable here, no effect on the diff**.
6. Commit trailers: the session-URL trailer plus a model-free co-author trailer (read on the branch commit 2e7bb5fb2) — **accepted**; pre-push accepted it and it matches AGENTS.md's trailer rule.
7. Zero label writes; `skip-changeset` not applicable because a patch changeset exists — **right**.
8. Run cut by a usage limit and resumed from the earlier branch state e49aaec73 without redoing work — **procedural; the net diff is judged, not the path to it**.

Out-of-scope findings
1. `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md:204-205` still says to stamp "`packages/spec/package.json` 的当前版本标签" (verified at the head) — **carried by #23057** (`Blocked-by: #23042`, per the claim), a Tier S edit that correctly does not ride this PR. **No action here.**
2. `packages/spec/scripts/build-retired-after-census.ts` header, "When to run it": tolerance written as `[last censused release, package.json label]` — **not shipped** (`scripts/` is not in `files[]`) and, read with semver precedence, still literally true (an `18.0.0-next.N` upper bound excludes `18.0.0`); it also defers to the test docblock, which now states the rule. **Imprecise, not wrong; no carrier owed. Recommend #23057's author tighten it to "release triple)" in passing.**
3. `metadata-core/src/artifact-forward-conversion.ts` docblock ("while the package label still names the last release of M-1") and `artifact-forward-conversion.test.ts:680-696` ("stamped at the prerelease label", meaning the label during the prerelease, `17.7.0`) — their stamp half states this rule; the "still names" clause is true until the first pre-mode version pass. **Agrees in substance; no carrier owed. Note for #23057's author only.**
4. `packages/metadata-core/CHANGELOG.md:489`, a released entry — **history; no action, right.**

My own sweep beyond the dev's (`git grep retiredAfter` at `origin/main`, every non-CHANGELOG hit): `docs/releases-maintenance.md:450` (refresh the census after a stable publish; states no stamp rule), `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx:1276` ("the last `@objectstack/spec` version that accepted the old shape"; agrees), `.changeset/23001-*` (agrees, quoted in ①), `.changeset/5082-*` (`declared-index-unique-scope` stamped `17.7.0`; agrees), `metadata/src/plugin.ts` (reads the door's result; no rule text). **No unflagged inconsistency.**

Governed surfaces: none of the 3 paths is in the register (no `.claude/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`); `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is success. This review is owed by the dispatch's path leg (`packages/spec/src/**`, non-test), and the file surface matches the claim's.

Check-runs on the head at 2026-10-13T03:01Z: 39 total — 23 success (among them `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, the four card/branch/single-writer claim checks), 6 skipped (opt-in and docs/console gates), 10 in progress (`Build Core`, `Test Core (1/6)` to `(6/6)`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace`). An in-progress run is not a pass: the landing waits for every one of them to conclude green. This verdict is on the contract in the diff, not on those runs.
